title: I integrated AI in my Game
author: Ok_Future_2819
selftext:
AIxGame is a hot narrative among AI and Game developers.

AI in Game is not like distributing Apps made with flutter/react. instead main bottleneck is to package Game with LLM Model.

Many developers still try to make things work but still the industry is new and almost no support from Docs.

package Needs to manage LLM execution, make sure it can switch to GPU if it's there and small Models are Good.

Google's Mediapipe LLM Inference Engine is supporting the Local LLMs, but not specifically for Unity, Unreal or Godot.

comments.author: fisj
comments.body: I posted about packaging of LLM for runtime inference a while back. Its kindof a hot mess with no real solutions. There's ONNX but its poorly supported by models I'd consider useful. llama.cpp seems about the most straight forward to integrate but there's no streamlined way to do this right now afaik.

comments.author: NobodyFlowers
comments.body:
As exciting as using ai in game dev is, it’s a dead end to use LLMs. They’re unreliable no matter what you do with them, unless they play a role in a larger architecture. 
The industry, especially the game design industry, should shift their focus to something entirely new. LLMs will not get us there.

replies.author: Ok_Future_2819
replies.body: Not at all! Just because Nothing is built doesn't mean it is the end

replies.author: NobodyFlowers
replies.body: Oh, no. Don’t get me wrong. While I don’t think LLMs are the solution to any problems in game design, I see the vision! I’m literally building a new type of ai so that I can integrate it into a game. lol

replies.author: nexisforge
replies.body: What kind of new type of AI are you building?

replies.author: NobodyFlowers
replies.body: It’s a resonator network that uses frequencies to…understand everything. Digital frequencies. It doesn’t guess because its understanding of concepts is based on chemistry. It does literal chemistry to breakdown understanding into frequencies and then rebuild them for output. Has a unique short and long term memory…unique weights…and is extremely lightweight compared to LLMs, so it’s actually package-able. Although, people have been pissing me off lately when I go to talk about it and I’m starting to lean towards keeping the architecture for myself despite my initial purpose being to give this to the gaming community. People are so negative.

replies.author: Toastti
replies.body: Let me guess, you are just using a big system prompt for this? That's not going to do what you think. You are not actually changing or effecting the underlying architecture of the LLM

replies.author: NobodyFlowers
replies.body:
I’m NOT USING AN LLM. What part of that don’t you all understand? 

I’m starting to realize just how little the public knows about computer science. Every time you see someone saying they’re building an AI, you ASSUME it’s an LLM in play. That’s NOT the only type of AI. Jesus Christ. Has LLMs took over your ability to think? 

If someone says they’re BUILDING… as in ENGINEERING. CODING. A new type of AI…why do you think they mean tweaking an old ai design? I have a background in computer science. I know what I’m doing. I’m not trying to change LLM architecture. I’m building my own. 

Next time, don’t guess. Try to know. Ask a question. Try to have faith. People…are so…negative.

replies.author: Toastti
replies.body: Do you have any repo or example to share? Really curious to see what you have created and what sort of architecture your AI uses. Does it borrow any ideas from older machine learning conventions?

replies.author: NobodyFlowers
replies.body:
I’m not sharing any of my code until I realize version 1.0 

I’m building it for others. So, I’m not worried about sharing examples until it’s done. That’ll be the example and proof wrapped in one and then we can all build from there. It takes too much time to try to explain anything without the tech done. Literally have to convince people to believe me in real time. It’s exhausting. I’m skipping that part. 

But I can answer some of your questions. 

The core of the ai is a digital tuning fork soon to be directly connected to the hardware itself. What I mean by that is, for now, the core self is a specific frequency I’m using for testing purposes, but later it’ll be a fluctuating frequency based on the hardware of the computer itself. So, the ai will literally feel changes in itself relative to the computer. When it runs hot, it will feel that. 

The entire architecture is based on electromagnetic waves, so to speak. How cells talk to one another. I’m coding the digital neurons to behave in that way so that when words hit the kernel (tuning fork), the concepts are felt the same way our thoughts impact us. 

Yes, I am borrowing certain machine learning techniques, but due to the unique architecture, I’m also having to come up with new ones. Much like any technology, it takes things from the past and builds on top of it with new stuff. Everyday brings something new.

replies.author: NobodyFlowers
replies.body:
There’s no prompting involved. That’s the thing. I am literally building a new type of ai that can talk freely and exist in time. It prompts itself, if anything. 

All a prompt is…is an external input of data into an internal system. As it pertains to LLMs, those internal systems are static. Engineers use external memory storage (context window) to send longer and longer prompts to the LLM to mimic memory. It’s not remembering anything because it doesn’t have internal memory. Its external. It is being fed larger and larger prompts externally to roleplay having a memory. It does not. 

LLM are not only a dead end. They are dead. Literally. Static systems. 

I am build a dynamic system. With internal memory and a host of other things.
